text: He is loading a whole ship with ice, and sailing it somewhere hot. Every sailor on the dock is laughing. Ice? To the tropics? It'll be soup before you leave the harbor! The captain shakes his head. Who in a hot country even wants ice? He just smiles and pats a sack of sawdust. Far away, on a hot island, his buddy is building a strange house. The walls are twice as thick as normal. No windows. Just one small door, and piles of sawdust inside. The trip takes weeks. Every day it gets hotter, and every day the crew checks the hold. Drip. Drip. Drip. Hey, ice man! Should we sell your cargo by the cup? It's so hot the cook fries eggs on the deck. But he isn't worried. He just keeps the hatch shut tight, and waits. The ship lands, and the ice is still solid. But the bar owners just shrug. Our drinks are warm, our beds are warm, we like warm! So he does something crazier. He gives the ice away. For free. You see, sawdust is full of tiny pockets of air, and air is terrible at carrying heat. It's the same trick a picnic cooler uses today. Packed tight, big blocks last for months, even under a tropical sun. One taste of an ice-cold drink in the heat, and the whole town is hooked. Every bar wants ice, every day. He builds more ice houses, more ships, more ice. Now everyone who laughed is buying his ice.
instructions: Casual YouTube Shorts storyteller. Warm, a little wry, quick, like telling a friend a weird true story at a bar. Clear, simple English. Do the quoted lines in character voices: a loud mocking sailor for 'Ice? To the tropics?' and 'Hey, ice man!', a dry gruff captain for 'Who in a hot country even wants ice?', and a lazy, sleepy bar owner who stretches out the word 'warm'. Say 'Drip. Drip. Drip.' slowly with small gaps. Build energy through 'The ship lands, and the ice is still solid.' Take a beat before 'So he does something crazier.' Drop a notch, calm and clear, for 'You see'. Short pause before the last line, then punch it.
